name: slurm-monitor-top
description: htop-style live view of Slurm jobs, nodes, GPUs and disks, in the sidebar or a full editor tab.

additionalProperties.markdownDescription: Where that cluster is: `here` for the machine this runs on, an ssh destination (`me@login01`), or a whole command line (`ssh -J jump login02`, `docker exec slurm slurm-top --json`).

slurmTop.servers.markdownDescription:
The clusters to watch, as name → where. The name labels the cluster in the tables; the address is one of:

- `here` — the machine this extension runs on, which under Remote - SSH is the host you are connected to. The row you start with. Rename it and that name is used; leave it and the panels show its hostname.
- `me@login01` — an ssh destination, as you would type it after `ssh`
- `ssh -J jump me@login02` — a whole ssh line, if it needs options; `slurm-top --json` is added for you when the line stops at the destination
- `docker exec slurm slurm-top --json` — any command that prints slurm-top JSON

Each row gets a collector process of its own, and their jobs, machines, GPUs and disks are merged into one view, tagged with the server they came from — see `#slurmTop.mergeServers#`. Remove a row to stop watching it; emptying the list altogether brings `here` back.

An ssh cluster needs slurm-monitor-top installed there, reachable from a *non-interactive* login (check with `ssh HOST slurm-top --json --help`; if it says command not found, give the full path or `python3 -m slurm_top.export` in the address), and a login that does not ask for a password: a bare destination is reached with `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`, so give it a key or an agent. **Slurm: Show Extension Log** reports what a failing command said.

slurmTop.mergeServers.markdownDescription: With several servers in `#slurmTop.servers#`, whether each section is one panel covering all of them (with a SERVER column) or one panel per server. Ignored while only one server is watched.

summary.description: One box of totals for everything, rather than one box per server.

jobs.description: One jobs table for every server, with a server column and a server filter.

nodes.description: One machines table for every server.

gpus.description: One GPU table, with each model's cards summed across the servers that have them.

disks.description: One disks table for every server.

slurmTop.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Python interpreter used to run the data collector. Empty means: try `python3`, then `python`. Ignored when `#slurmTop.command#` is set, and once `#slurmTop.servers#` has anything in it.

slurmTop.command.markdownDescription: Full command that emits slurm-top JSON, as an argv array (for example `["ssh", "login01", "slurm-top", "--json"]`). Data-mode flags such as `--watch` are appended. Empty means auto-detect. Describes the single fallback server, and is ignored once `#slurmTop.servers#` has anything in it.

slurmTop.pauseWhenHidden.description: Stop polling the cluster while no Slurm view is visible.

slurmTop.sidebarSections.description: Sections shown in the narrow sidebar view, in order. Panels there can be collapsed by clicking their header. The dashboard always shows all of them.

slurmTop.defaultOwnerFilter.description: Which jobs the sidebar shows on open.

enumDescriptions: A floating window of its own, like Settings moved out of the main window: resizable, movable, and can sit on a second monitor.
A floating list over the editor, like the command palette: type to filter the fields, Enter to copy one, Escape to dismiss.
A card centred in an editor tab, dimming the rest of that tab.
A plain editor tab beside your code, which stays open while you work.
A panel inside the Slurm view you clicked in.
slurmTop.detailsIn.markdownDescription: Where job and machine details open. `window` needs VS Code 1.85 or later and falls back to `tab` on older builds.

slurmTop.cpuProbeUsesSrun.markdownDescription: When reading a machine's CPU model, fall back to a one-second Slurm job if ssh to that node is refused. Slurm reports neither the model nor the clock, so one of the two routes is the only way to get them. Turn this off to try ssh only, on clusters where submitting a probe job is unwelcome. Probes only ever run when you ask for one.
